problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 13 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Euclidean Spaces (Arbitrary Bases): Applications

feedback.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1+1\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{3},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
